fix: show current month/year data on dashboard when no prior DayStatistics exist (issue #2148)

On the first day of a new month or year, period_totals() skipped the
today_stats merge for every key because the historical aggregate was None.
The dashboard month and year panels showed nothing all day as a result.

Treat a None aggregate as 0 when today has a value, so live consumption
on the first day of a new period flows through as-is.

Same root cause and fix as issue #1944 (MQTT period totals), now applied
to the dashboard path as well.

fix: eliminate midnight-border gap in daily and hourly electricity totals (issue #1770)

day_consumption() and create_hourly_statistics() previously anchored on the
first/last ElectricityConsumption record *within* each window, silently dropping
the interval between adjacent windows.  Replace with cross-boundary anchor
queries (last record strictly before the window start/end) for gap-free totals.

Also rewrites dsmr_backend/tests/test_statistics_integration.py from scratch:
seed reading before the data window, tighter electricity assertions (places=3),
dedicated test_midnight_border_gap test, DSMR v4 boundary reading to cover the
last hour whose gas entry is shifted back by _compact_gas().

Closes issue #1770.

docs: add v6.2.0 changelog entry for MQTT period totals midnight-window fix (issue #1811)

fix: publish MQTT period totals on first day of new month/year (issue #1944)

When no DayStatistics exist yet for the current month or year (e.g. all
of January 1st), period_totals() was skipping the today_stats merge for
every key because the historical aggregate was None.  The result dict
came back entirely empty, causing both JSON and split-topic MQTT
publishers to silently suppress all period-total messages for the day.

Treat a None aggregate as 0 when today has a value, so that live
consumption on the first day of a new period flows through as-is.

fix: use lte/bisect_right so EC records at exact hour boundaries are used as anchors - #1770

In minute-grouped mode, ElectricityConsumption records are written at exact
minute boundaries (e.g. EC@10:00:00 = meter position at start of hour 10).
Both create_hourly_statistics() and recalculate_hour_statistics() used
read_at__lt / bisect_left semantics which excluded records at the boundary
itself, causing each hour's anchors to be off by one minute.

Fix: use read_at__lte in create_hourly_statistics() and recalculate_hour_statistics()
(including the ec_in_window window-end filter), and bisect_right instead of
bisect_left in recalculate_hour_statistics() so that a record at exactly
hour_start or hour_end is selected as the anchor rather than the preceding one.

test: add midnight anchor reading so every UTC hour has a closing EC boundary - #1770

The lte fix for create_hourly_statistics() exposed that the last UTC hour of
Jan 11 (22:00-23:00) had no closing EC anchor, causing it to compute 0.001
instead of the expected 0.002. Adding a reading at AMS Jan 12 00:00 (UTC Jan 11
23:00) provides that anchor and makes the integration test data complete.

fix: cast DecimalField int values to float before writing to InfluxDB (#2174)

When a meter is replaced, all counters reset to 0. Django's __dict__ bypasses
the DecimalField descriptor, so 0 arrives as a Python int rather than a Decimal.
The InfluxDB client serialises int as "0i" (integer line-protocol type), which
conflicts with the existing float field type and causes all subsequent writes to
be rejected with a field type conflict error.

fix: skip Buienradar station fetch when weather tracking is disabled (#2148)

When tracking is disabled, get_buienradar_stations() now returns an empty
list immediately without making an API call or logging a warning. The admin
form pins the current station as a valid choice so saves succeed without
requiring a live station list.

chore(deps): resolve dependencies with uv, keep poetry.lock in sync

Poetry's resolver can run out of memory when a constraint change forces
real re-resolution. pyproject.toml now declares dependencies via the
standard PEP 621/PEP 735 tables so both Poetry and uv can read them; uv
does the actual resolving (uv.lock), and scripts/sync_poetry_lock.py
regenerates poetry.lock from that without ever invoking Poetry's own
resolver. Poetry itself still only installs/runs, unchanged.
